newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EU gets WTO dispute panel on U.S. anti-Cuba law.
newsitem.headline: EU gets WTO dispute panel on U.S. anti-Cuba law.

text.p: The World Trade Organisation on Wednesday agreed to a European Union request to set up a panel to decide whether the United States Helms-Burton law on Cuba violates WTO rules, officials said.
The decision, taken by the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) in whose shaping Washington played a key role, was automatic after U.S. trade diplomats blocked an earlier EU request last month.

In its submission, the EU argues that the law -- which aims at reducing investment by other countries in communist-ruled Cuba and has been widely condemned by nearly all U.S. trade partners -- runs counter to a range of WTO rules.

U.S. trade envoys have indicated that they will argue the measure -- approved by President Bill Clinton as he began campaigning for re-election early this year -- is covered by a WTO "national security" clause.

This untested provision, part of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade which underpins the two-year-old trade body, suggests a member of the WTO -- to which 125 countries now belong -- can ignore the rules if it sees its security at stake.

Many trade analysts fear a panel finding, likely in around seven months, would risk seriously damaging the fledgling WTO whichever way it goes. The EU, backed by Canada and Mexico among others, argues Washington is trying to impose its own political views on others by using trade muscle.
